subject: HealthMesh DPA — trained-model restrictions, subprocessor gating, and operator roles
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthMesh DPA — trained-model restrictions, subprocessor gating, and operator roles

Team — heads-up: HealthMesh sent back a DPA draft with an explicit prohibition on any model improvement (no-training) and an ask that any subprocessors be "gated at the operator/role level" (they want a named list of human reviewers and whether any human-in-the-loop could see prompts/responses). They also want on-prem forwarding rules called out if we ever proxy through a customer-managed endpoint.

Key asks from legal/procurement:
- Confirm we can commit to no-training on tenant interactions (they want an auditable ops path).
- Provide an operator matrix: which Redwood roles (SRE, Support, Ops, Data Steward) can access plaintext prompts/responses and under what controls.
- Describe subprocessor gating: how do we prevent subprocessors from using data for training, and which subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers for logging/metrics) are in scope.
- On-prem / VPC: they want a clause that if traffic is routed via a customer-managed connector (on-prem or VPC peering) we will not persist tenant data beyond ephemeral caches.

I attached their redline and a quick operator-matrix I sketched. Can David and Ben please confirm operational feasibility + what evidence/controls we can offer (audit logs, KMS scoping, ephemeral KV configs, role-based access)? Lauren, can you weigh in on acceptable legal language we can offer without breaking our product commitments?

Goal: reply to Olivia (cc procurement) with a clear list of controls and an implementation timeline by EOD today so we can keep the commercial cadence.

Thanks —
Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthMesh DPA — trained-model restrictions, subprocessor gating, and operator roles

Marissa — thanks for the summary. Quick operational notes:

1) No-training (model improvement) commitment: we can offer a contractual "no-model-improvement" guarantee for tenant interactions if the customer selects the non-improve flag on their tenant and uses either (a) Hosted with explicit opt-out enabled or (b) Dedicated/Private where the capture path is controlled. Implementation: add a platform toggle record + audit log entry; engineering time ~2 sprints to add attestation metadata and exportable audit CSV. Evidence: we can provide an "ops snapshot" export showing the flag and sampling of audit logs for a short window.

2) Operator matrix: attached XLSX covers role names and read vs redact vs never-access categories. Short summary:
- Support Tier 1: sanitized metadata only (no raw prompts)
- SRE/Infra: encrypted keys/metrics only; no prompt access by default
- Data Steward: access via approval workflow (2 approvers) and session-recorded review

3) Subprocessor gating: our current subprocessors (cloud storage, metrics pipeline, monitoring) can be scoped per-tenant for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we can scope log export and use encryption-at-rest with tenant-scoped KMS keys. We cannot feasibly enumerate every sub-subcontractor in a redline, but we can provide a subprocessor inventory and a gating attest (we control whether logs reach third-party analytics).

4) On-prem connector: for VPC/on-prem we can document ephemeral caching only and a maximum retention SLA for forwarded traffic; we should avoid wording that implies we will never persist (we do persist short-lived KV caches for inference efficiency). Suggest phrase: "data forwarded to customer-managed endpoints will be treated as ephemeral by Redwood and retained only as required for active inference with configurable retention controls."

I'll join a call with HealthMesh if needed. I estimate we can produce a formal evidence packet (subprocessor inventory + operator access screenshots + sample audit CSV) within 5 business days.

-David
Director, Security & Privacy Operations
(attachment referenced: operator access matrix)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthMesh DPA — trained-model restrictions, subprocessor gating, and operator roles

Marissa / team — adding notes from product/ops perspective so replies are concrete:

- Flagging scope: we can guarantee "no-model-improvement" only for interactions that are correctly labeled tenant_interaction=true and when the customer does not enable telemetry exports. For Hosted customers, we need an explicit tenant-level opt-out API and a UI toggle; tagging must be deterministic.
- Evidence we can deliver: audit logs (who accessed which session_id), ephemeral cache TTL settings per tenant, and KMS key usage logs (Cloud KMS audit).
- Human review flow: we have an approval workflow (Jira-based) today for Data Steward reviews — we can export approval history as evidence. If HealthMesh insists on a "named" human list in contract, we should push back: instead propose role-based commitments + a CSV of named individuals at signing that we update quarterly.
- Subprocessor list: provide current list + commit to notify for new subprocessors 30 days prior.

Recommend reply: propose two paths — Hosted w/ explicit opt-out (fast, with limited evidence pack) or Dedicated/Private (full operator gating, per-tenant KMS, stronger evidence). Ask what they prefer and offer a 1-week evidence delivery SLA for Dedicated.

-ben
Senior Product Manager, Inference Platform

Follow-ups: 
- Can Redwood provide a short evidence packet (subprocessor inventory PDF, operator-role CSV, sample audit export) by next Thursday?
- For the contract language, procurement will accept a role-based commitment + quarterly named roster as Ben suggested. Please include the suggested DocuSign-ready clause for: (a) no-model-improvement for tenant interactions, (b) KMS scoping and onshore residency for key material, and (c) 30-day notice for adding subprocessors with a right to object for material changes.

We attached their redline earlier — we can accept the operator roster quarterly cadence. If you can produce the evidence pack and the drafting language, procurement will prepare the final SOW and routing for signature.

Olivia Grant
